section_summary: This section contains U.S. military intelligence compilations from the European Theater, beginning with the final portion of report Serial J-058 (pages 68–101) and continuing with a series of Japanese Document Reports, Serials CD-124 through CD-135 (pages 102–123). Serial J-058 presents technical data and field interrogations of prominent German industrialists and engineers evaluating Japan's synthetic fuel, nitrogen, sulfuric acid, and chemical weapon capabilities, as well as the relative vulnerability of chemical plants and railway links to Allied strategic bombing. The subsequent G-2 reports index captured German and Japanese records seized from Rheinmetall-Borsig, industrial representatives, and the Japanese Embassy in Berlin, detailing arms deliveries, aircraft licensing, cultural propaganda films, cartographic holdings, and diplomatic-military files.

subfiles.about: Concludes an intelligence survey of Japanese synthetic fuels and chemical production, incorporating technical field reports and interrogations of German chemical executives to assess strategic bombing targets.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: This concluding segment (pages 16–32 and appendices) of report Serial J-058 evaluates the Japanese five-year synthetic fuel expansion plan, covering coal hydrogenation, Fischer-Tropsch synthesis, and Fushun shale oil operations, accompanied by technical reflections from Lurgi engineer Dr. Hubmann and DEGUSSA chemical process sales records. Statistical tables detail synthetic and byproduct nitrogen plant capacities, processes, and outputs across Japan proper, Korea, and Manchuria, alongside an index of German industrial personnel interrogated. The appendices compile reports and interrogation transcripts from U.S. Strategic Bombing Survey (USSBS) Field Team 78, including interviews with Karl Krauch, Walter Steinle, Karl Braus, Karl Graessle, Dir. Clemm, and Dr. Klebert concerning synthetic ammonia, nitric acid, methanol, soda ash, and sulfuric acid production. German experts consistently recommend primary ammonia fixation facilities and concentrated nitric acid works over synthetic fuel installations as the most critical and vulnerable targets for strategic bombing, while also noting German shipments of ethylene dibromide for Japanese tetraethyllead synthesis.
subfiles.title: Serial J-058: Report on Japanese Synthetic Oil, Chemical Industries, and Target Vulnerability
subfiles.to: Distribution (Allied Intelligence Agencies: War Department, War Office, Admiralty, C.N.O., Air Ministry, USGCC, USSTAF, etc.)

subfiles.about: Catalogs captured records of Rheinmetall-Borsig A.G. in Apolda documenting weapons deliveries, technical blueprints, and manufacturing rights provided to Japan.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: Reports on corporate records seized on 23 May 1945 at Apolda by 12th Army Group interrogators covering armaments delivered to Japan by Rheinmetall-Borsig A.G. between 1941 and 1945. The inventory enumerates shipped hardware, blueprints, tooling specifications, and production time schedules for MG 131 aircraft machine guns, 2 cm anti-aircraft guns, 10.5 cm heavy anti-aircraft guns, and aviation bombs ranging from 2 kg incendiaries to 1,400 kg high explosives. The report notes that Rheinmetall director Wilhelm Warnecke stated Germany gifted Japan all rights and patents for the Panzerfaust anti-tank weapon, information confirmed by Otto Bräutigam.
subfiles.title: Serial CD-124: Germany, Supply of Armaments to Japan (Rheinmetall-Borsig A.G., Apolda)

subfiles.about: Describes captured ledgers, correspondence, and accounts of the Japanese Embassy, consulates, and the Yokohama Specie Bank in Berlin.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: Indexes financial records, loose accounting notes, notebooks, and ledgers running through April 1945 seized at the Japanese Embassy in Berlin in July 1945 by the USFET Japanese Intelligence Section. The collection documents financial transactions and bank accounts maintained by Japanese diplomatic missions in Germany and the Yokohama Specie Bank, as well as monetary dealings involving Spain and Portugal. The original records were designated for transmittal to MIRS Washington via London.
subfiles.title: Serial CD-125: Germany, Japanese Financial Transactions in

subfiles.about: Indexes 26 reels of Japanese cultural documentary films produced by Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai captured at the Japanese Embassy in Berlin.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: Catalogs 26 motion picture film reels produced between 1936 and 1939 by the Society for International Cultural Relations (Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai, Tokyo) and seized at the Japanese Embassy in Berlin on 4 August 1945. The educational and cultural documentaries cover Japanese primary schools, deep-sea fishing, floral arrangement, classical painters, cormorant fishing, winter sports, seasonal landscapes, folk handcrafts, and festivals, alongside travelogues of Tokyo, Kyoto, Nara, Peking, and Nagoya. The physical films were processed by USFET Documents Center for delivery to MIRS Washington.
subfiles.title: Serial CD/126: Japan, Cultural films of

subfiles.about: Documents the capture and disposition of two Japanese typewriters seized from the Japanese Embassy in Berlin.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: Records the seizure of two Japanese typewriters recovered from the Japanese Embassy in Berlin in July 1945 by the Japanese Intelligence Section, USFET. The captured items were transferred to the USFET Documents Center for transmission to MIRS Washington.
subfiles.title: Serial CD-127: Japanese Typewriters

subfiles.about: Lists photograph albums, loose photographs, negatives, and motion picture film reels recovered from the Japanese Embassy in Berlin.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: Inventories visual materials captured on 9 August 1945 at the Japanese Embassy in Berlin by the USFET Japanese Intelligence Section. The items comprise thirteen photograph albums, a box of photographic negatives, three envelopes of loose prints, several motion picture reels of German and Japanese personalities, and a German technical aviation film on the Jumo 211 engine. The materials were routed via A-2, USSTAF, Tempelhof, to MIRS London and Washington.
subfiles.title: Serial CD-128: Germany, Japanese Embassy, Miscellaneous photographs and Personalities of

subfiles.about: Catalogs captured records of Ernst Prieger, representative of Fujihara Shoji Kaisha in Berlin, detailing Japanese negotiations and technical ties with German aircraft firms.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: Indexes extensive correspondence, contracts, and notes from 1938 to 1945 seized around 18 August 1945 from the Berlin home and office of Ernst Prieger, representative of Fujihara Shoji Kaisha. The documents record Japanese military and commercial inquiries, licensing agreements, and deliveries involving major German aviation manufacturers including Heinkel (He 112), Junkers (Ju 86, Ju 88, diesel aero-engines, variable-pitch propellers), Fieseler (Fi 156 Storch), Focke-Wulf (Fw 200 Condor, Ta 152), Siebel (Si 204), Messerschmitt (Bf 109, Me 210, Me 163, Me 262), and Gothaer Waggonfabrik (DFS 230 gliders, Go 242, Go 244). Related files document deliveries of I.G. Farben synthetic aircraft glues (Kauritleim), Schwarz wooden propellers, Goerz bomb sights and navigation equipment, and Argus and Bosch aircraft components.
subfiles.title: Serial CD-129: Japanese Contacts with German Aircraft Firms

subfiles.about: Details captured files regarding deliveries of German heavy machine tools, optical glass, and specialized alloy steels to the Japanese Army.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: Summarizes commercial correspondence and invoices from 1939 to 1944 captured in July 1945 at the Japanese Embassy in Berlin concerning deliveries to the Japanese Army. Transactions were handled by trading houses Mitsui Bussan, Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha, and Showa Tsusho, working through German suppliers such as Schuchardt & Schütte, Hahn & Kolb, and Messerschmitt. Procurements covered heavy industrial machinery (forging presses, hammers, lathes, milling machines, grinding equipment, and diamond tools) alongside optical glass, measuring instruments, and specialized aviation steels including nickel-chrome and propeller steel.
subfiles.title: Serial CD-130: Germany, Commercial Relations with Japan

subfiles.about: Documents the capture and evacuation of books, dictionaries, and reference publications from the library of the Japanese Embassy in Berlin.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: Records the seizure in July 1945 of multiple cases of Japanese and German published books, reference dictionaries, and library volumes from the Japanese Embassy in Berlin. The collection was processed by the USFET Japanese Intelligence Section and forwarded via the USFET Documents Center and MIRS London to MIRS Washington.
subfiles.title: Serial CD-131: Germany, Japanese Embassy Library in

subfiles.about: Catalogs a comprehensive inventory of military, geographic, industrial, and demographic maps seized from the Japanese Embassy in Berlin.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: Provides an itemized catalog of maps captured in July 1945 at the Japanese Embassy in Berlin by the USFET Japanese Intelligence Section. The collection includes a multi-sheet Japanese-character map of Chinese administrative divisions and cities, German military and general maps of Russia, the Near East, Eastern Europe, and Scandinavia, and French fortification plans as of August 1939. Additionally, the inventory details Russian thematic interpretive charts covering industry, population, agriculture, and transportation, alongside British physical charts and multi-lingual map sheets.
subfiles.title: Serial CD-132: Japanese, German, Russian, Polish, Italian Maps

subfiles.about: Indexes correspondence, diplomatic cables, attaché diaries, and personnel files seized from the Japanese Military and Naval Attachés in Berlin.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: Catalogs official papers dating from 1941 to 1945 captured in Berlin during July 1945 from the offices of the Japanese Military and Naval Attachés. Holdings include incoming and outgoing telegrams, registers and passport files of Japanese residents in Germany, records of the 1941 Naval Commission, and Luftwaffe travel passes issued for official travel to Japan in 1945. Also indexed are contracts and receipts for 1944-1945 procurements of arms and machine tools, along with personal diaries of attaché personnel, including Nakamura and Otani.
subfiles.title: Serial CD-133: Miscellaneous Papers of the Japanese Military and Naval Attache's, Berlin

subfiles.about: Details captured contracts, technical manuals, and correspondence regarding advanced German aircraft, guided weapon mechanisms, and aviation technology acquired by Japan.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: Inventories technical files and procurement contracts dating from 1939 to 1945 captured in August 1945 from the Military (Air) Attaché's office at the Japanese Embassy in Berlin. Documents cover sales conditions and delivery specifications for five Focke-Wulf Fw 200 C-5 aircraft, DFS 230 gliders, Messerschmitt Me 210s, Ju 88 bombers, and Fw 190 fighters, as well as inquiries by Vice-Admiral Toyoda and Major General Otani to inspect the Messerschmitt Me 262 jet fighter. Records also describe remote-control firing installations (Junkers FA 15 and Rheinmetall FDL 131 Z), MK 108 cannon charging valves, Zeiss gunsights, Lotfe 7 H bombsights, BMW 801 engines, Lorenz blind-landing gear, and miscellaneous embassy architectural plans and economic surveys.
subfiles.title: Serial CD-134: Japanese Interest in German Air Equipment

subfiles.about: Inventories economic, financial, and industrial reports and accounting statements seized from the Japanese Embassy in Berlin.
subfiles.from: Office of Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, Headquarters, U.S. Forces, European Theater (Main)
subfiles.summary: Catalogs economic, industrial, and financial records dating from 1941 to 1945 captured in July 1945 at the Japanese Embassy in Berlin by the USFET Japanese Intelligence Section. The documents include general economic reviews of Japan for 1941-1942, financial statements for machinery deliveries in 1942, liquefaction plant accounts from 1941, shipping lists from 1944, and an invoice book for 1945. Additional files cover correspondence regarding commercial representatives and firms (including Hishihira and Sakura) and exchange/finance data from 1943.
subfiles.title: Serial CD-135: Economics and Industrial Reports on Japan
